topic: Are you the same person you were ten years ago?

messages.speaker: kierkegaard
messages.content:
The question is asked as if identity were a fact to be checked, like the register of a parish. But the self is not a fact; the self is a task. A relation that relates itself to itself, I wrote in The Sickness Unto Death, and most people never take up the relation at all. They are a mood at twenty, a position at thirty, a pension at fifty, and they call this sequence 'I' out of politeness.

So my answer must be a question, as usual, aimed at that single individual reading over our shoulders: have you ever chosen yourself? Not improved yourself, the age adores improvement, but chosen: taken over your own history, guilt included, as yours. The man who has done this is more the same across ten years than a stone is, because his continuity is earned nightly. The man who has not is not even the same person across an afternoon.

messages.speaker: beauvoir
messages.content:
Søren makes the self a private drama between a man and his despair; I keep the theater but insist on the scenery. One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman: my most quoted sentence, and its point is that becoming is not a solitary leap. It happens in a body that ages, in institutions that assign roles, under gazes that harden into mirrors. Ask the woman of fifty whether she is the girl of forty years earlier and she will answer truly: yes, and no, and the no was partly done to her.

The self is a project thrown toward the future, so of course I am not the same as ten years ago; sameness would mean the project had stopped, which is one definition of despair we can share, Søren. But I add what your parish register omits: some people are denied the materials of becoming. Their situation freezes them into repetition and then philosophy scolds them for lacking depth. Before asking whether you are the same person, ask who was permitted to change.

messages.speaker: zhuxi
messages.content:
In my school we would find this talk of leaps and dramas somewhat feverish. Consider instead the mirror, an image my tradition has polished for centuries, and note what the leap-makers skip: polishing is slow. The principle in you, your original nature, does not change in ten years or ten thousand; it is the same pattern, li, that threads all things. What changes is the turbidity of the endowment through which it shines. Study, reverent attention, the investigation of things, one today, another tomorrow: this is how the shining clears.

So: are you the same person? Your pattern, yes. Your clarity, I hope not. The Great Learning speaks of renewing the people daily; the bathtub of King Tang bore the inscription: if you can one day renew yourself, do so from day to day. Renewal is not replacement. The man who claims to have become someone else has usually just changed his clothes; the man who has read seriously for ten years is recognizably himself, only less in his own way.

messages.speaker: wang-yangming
messages.content:
Master Zhu, your mirror is right and your method wrong, as I found the hard way. I followed your teaching as a young man: sat before bamboo for seven days to investigate its principle, and harvested nothing but a fever. The principle was never in the bamboo. The mind itself is principle, and the innate knowing, liangzhi, was complete in me at seven and at seventy, complete in the bandit I pardoned and in the student who betrayed me.

So to the question I say: in what matters most you are exactly the same person, and this is not consolation but indictment. The knowing that told you at twelve that cruelty is cruel tells you the same today; ten years cannot improve it, only bury it deeper under clever excuses or clear away the burial. Søren, your 'choosing yourself' I recognize: it is what I call making the knowing and the acting one. But it is not a leap in fear and trembling. It is simpler and more embarrassing: you already know what to do. The decade's question is only whether you did it.

messages.speaker: kierkegaard
messages.content:
Simpler and more embarrassing: General, I concede the embarrassing half. Yes, the evasion is the constant; I have written a whole authorship about the ways a man postpones what he already understands. But I cannot give you the simple half, and the mother in the crowd is my witness. When the command of the age, of the family, of the church itself says one thing and something absolute says another, the knowing is not sitting quietly inside like your liangzhi, legible and calm. Abraham rode three days to Moriah and could not explain himself to anyone. If the moral knowledge were innate and shared, he could have explained. The deepest choices are made where explanation ends; that is why I keep the fear and the trembling.

And Madame de Beauvoir, your correction I accept with less struggle: my single individual has always been read by those with the leisure to have a self-crisis. Let me return the gift. Your frozen ones, denied the materials of becoming: the age will offer them therapy and programs. You and I both know what they are actually owed first: to be addressed as a self at all, capable of inwardness, not as a case. Even the situation-bound person despairs, which is the grimmest proof of spirit I know.

messages.speaker: beauvoir
messages.content:
Owed to be addressed as a self, yes, but owed bread and contraception and literacy in the same breath, Søren, or the address is a courtesy paid to a prisoner. Spirit proves itself in despair; freedom proves itself in what it can actually undertake. I will not choose between the two sentences, and that refusal is my entire ethics of ambiguity.

And the two masters of the mirror, hear how your quarrel sounds from my century. Zhu Xi says polish slowly through study; Wang says the brightness was always there, act on it now. Every liberation movement I watched ran on both: the long patient clarification, reading, organizing, understanding the situation, and then the day someone acts on what she suddenly admits she always knew. Ten years, then. You are the same person in this sense: the debts you contracted with yourself remain in your name. You are a different person in this sense: what you can undertake has changed, and so has what you can no longer plead ignorance of. The question is not sameness. It is whether the decade left you with better excuses or fewer.
